newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's BUX falls one percent in profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's BUX falls one percent in profit-taking.

text.p: Hungarian shares fell on Thursday as a number of investors decided that it was time to unload their papers after a roughly 40 percent rise of the index since the beginning of the year, traders said.
The BUX index fell one percent or 57.56 points from Wednesday's record to close at 5,757.82.
"Certain investors have speeded up their profit-taking activities," said Robert Cselovszki of WestLB Investment.
Selling might have been driven partly by the fact that some investors believed that 1996 corporate results could be weaker than earlier expected.
"I think investors are cashing profits in," another trader said earlier today.
Traders said, however, it was too early to say whether today's fall and yesterday's intraday profit-taking was a correction before new rallies or was the beginning of a reverse.
"These two days were not enough to judge whether this is a turning point or a correction," Cselovszki said. "I can imagine further falls due to profit-taking."
Profit-taking slashed the price of oil and gas company MOL shares the most as they plunged almost three and a half percent to end at 3,500 forints, down 125.
Some stocks bucked the trend and hit new highs.
Hotel firm Danubius broke a new record of 6,145 forints, rising 440, as expectations of a strong 1996 continued to bolster its price, traders said.

Holding company Skala-Coop Rt jumped to a record level in early trading on Thursday after Skala had announced its plans to increase its stake to 41 percent from 25 percent in retail chain Centrum Aruhazak Rt.
Skala surged to a record high of 2,700 forints, but as trading resumed in it after a 10 minute suspension due to an over 10 percent intraday rise, it came down to close at 2,600, up 160.
"The rise is certainly in connection with the Centrum news," one trader said earlier today.
